architecture_decisions: The architecture decision involves adding a narrow server-owned authorization service adjacent to existing repository authority composition. This service resolves the Project's repository through existing owner-scoped authority, requires `github:owner/repository`, and constructs only: - connector: released server-owned `github/parallax-runtime` configuration; - subject: `{ "type": "app" }`; - `authorizationDetails`: exact one-repository GitHub App installation authorization generated from existing policy; - bounded server-chosen expiration; - no client-defined return URL, webhook, prompt, installation ID, scopes/resources or additional parameters. Provider timeout/request failure, non-2xx response, malformed body, missing URL/expiry, or unsafe URL fails closed. Raw provider payloads are not returned or durably persisted.
work_items: Implement the server-owned authorization service as a new component within the existing repository authority composition. This service should be responsible for resolving the Project's repository through existing owner-scoped authority, requiring `github:owner/repository`, and constructing only the necessary authorization details.
validations: Validate that the server-owned authorization service correctly resolves the Project's repository through existing owner-scoped authority, requires `github:owner/repository`, and constructs only the necessary authorization details. This validation should be performed using automated tests and manual verification.
AC-01: validate protected requirement — Only an authenticated owner can initiate repository authorization for a Project, and repository identity is resolved exclusively from canonical Project state.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — The authorization service always uses the released GitHub connector and fixed exact-repository GitHub App authorization detail. Browser input cannot alter connector, repository or authority.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Authorization initiation uses request/deployment-scoped Vercel OIDC and introduces no PAT, reusable personal token, user credential or persisted provider bearer.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Only the fixed Connect authorization endpoint is called with bounded timeout/no redirect following. Timeout, transport error, non-2xx or malformed response fails closed.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Only a bounded HTTPS consent URL on the explicit provider origin allowlist is returned. Malicious scheme, userinfo, foreign host/port, malformed or oversized URL is rejected.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — The API returns only status, validated authorization URL and normalized expiry. Provider request/verifier IDs, raw payloads and tokens are not returned or durably stored.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — The autonomy client receives `REPOSITORY_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED` as a bounded structured code without message parsing. Generic provider failures cannot trigger repository-consent UI.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Creating/opening a consent request does not mutate Project repository source, Engineering Run state/revision, Work Specification, lineage, deployment or REVIEW state.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — A typed read-only provider operation deterministically distinguishes existing commit-bearing, existing empty and missing/unauthorized repositories under exact repository scope.
AC-10: validate protected requirement — Provider outage, 404/403, credential failure, malformed response or ordinary `SOURCE_NOT_FOUND` alone cannot initialize greenfield lineage.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — A dedicated greenfield initialization operation can create a root lineage with zero files and canonical empty digest/provenance. Ordinary repository/template/starter packages remain non-empty by contract.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — Zero-file manifests/materialization are accepted only for a root `greenfield` lineage with exact invariants; forged empty implementation/non-greenfield lineage is rejected.
AC-13: validate protected requirement — IMPLEMENT must produce at least one protected source file and a changed non-root implementation lineage before BUILD/TEST/VERIFY can pass.

AC-14: validate protected requirement — PLAN through VERIFY on an empty repository performs no GitHub commit/ref/source mutation. Tests prove the initialization write action cannot be invoked before verified REVIEW delivery.

AC-15: validate protected requirement — At REVIEW, the fixed GitHub initialization action can create an empty tree, zero-parent provenance-bound commit and default-branch ref without force, and exact read-back proves the result.

AC-16: validate protected requirement — Retry reuses an existing baseline only if commit message/identity, zero parents, empty tree, Project/run/root lineage and default ref match exactly. Any unrelated head fails closed.

AC-17: validate protected requirement — After baseline initialization, accepted implementation is committed on the bounded Parallax branch from that baseline, not on default, and existing PR read-back semantics prove exact head/base identity.

AC-18: validate protected requirement — Vercel Preview is created from the exact accepted implementation commit and existing Preview read-back proves repository/source revision/target identity before delivery evidence is accepted.

AC-19: validate protected requirement — Greenfield delivery records exact initialization, branch, accepted commit, PR and Preview provider/audit evidence without raw credentials/provider payloads and remains replay-safe.

AC-20: validate protected requirement — Web/mobile surfaces show an accessible `Authorize repository` action only for the exact consent condition and preserve same-run `Try again`, current progress and saved work.

AC-21: validate protected requirement — After mocked/provider-approved consent, the same Engineering Run retries through the ordinary scoped token exchange and exact-one-repository GitHub verification before greenfield inspection/source authority is accepted.
AC-22: validate protected requirement — Canceled, expired, wrong-repository or incomplete consent never marks Project/repository ready and does not create greenfield lineage/source mutation.

AC-23: validate protected requirement — Commit-bearing public bootstrap, Python acceptance, OT Time .NET source-only acceptance, repository-root lineage, ordinary GitHub branch/commit/PR delivery, delivery-mode behavior, snapshots and REVIEW ceiling remain green.

AC-24: validate protected requirement — Runtime/provider/client code does not inspect Decision Ledger identity or target name; change cannot grant all-repository authority, arbitrary source mutation, production promotion, work approval or REVIEW completion.

AC-25: validate protected requirement — Before semantic release is treated as viable, a non-mutating preview/runtime diagnostic proves production-style OIDC can create the exact-repository Connect authorization request and the returned URL passes the released validator. Request/verifier values are not printed and diagnostic code is removed before merge.

AC-26: validate protected requirement — After explicit exact-repository consent, the canonical Decision Ledger trial proceeds without out-of-band source edits through greenfield root, accepted source, protected BUILD/TEST/VERIFY, bounded GitHub branch/PR publication, Vercel Preview and REVIEW, with exact evidence recorded.

AC-27: validate protected requirement — If consent, empty initialization, implementation, provider delivery or Preview exposes another boundary, it is recorded and separately governed rather than weakening gates.

AC-28: validate protected requirement — This exact spec obtains authentic DSPy SpecCritic + SpecCompiler evidence before semantic implementation. Final exact head passes protected spec validation, focused/full API tests, client/browser acceptance, Bounded Autonomy, protected promotion evaluation and applicable release gates before merge/deployment.
risks: The risk associated with the server-owned authorization service is the potential for unauthorized access to the Project's repository. This risk can be mitigated by implementing strict access controls and monitoring the service for any suspicious activity.

critique: The specification does not explicitly address the requirement for a governed zero-source greenfield root that can be created without an existing parent commit. This omission could lead to issues in the production environment where the greenfield root is not properly initialized, potentially causing data loss or inconsistencies.
